We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\csc x-14{x}^{3}+\cos x) \\  & =(-\csc x\cot x)-14\cdot 3{x}^{2}+(-\sin x) \\  & =-\csc x\cot x-42{x}^{2}-\sin x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-\csc \,(\frac{\pi }{4})\cot \,(\frac{\pi }{4})-42{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}-\sin \,(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot 1-42\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\sqrt{2}-\frac{21}{8}{\pi }^{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{21}{8}{\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
